summary: Explains that Ansible creates an implicit `localhost` when you reference one not defined in inventory (for example with `delegate_to: localhost` or `local_action`), using `ansible_connection: local` and `ansible_python_interpreter: {{ansible_playbook_python}}`. Defining `localhost` in inventory overrides this and makes it a normal host with its own vars.
questions: Do I need to put localhost in my inventory to delegate tasks to it?
What connection and Python does the implicit localhost use?
Why did my delegate_to localhost start using SSH after I added localhost to inventory?
How do I override the implicit localhost settings?
Which Python interpreter runs tasks delegated to localhost?

answer_card.title: Implicit localhost
answer_card.answer_md:
If you reference `localhost` (e.g. `delegate_to: localhost` or `local_action`) without defining it in inventory, Ansible creates one, equivalent to:

```yaml
hosts:
  localhost:
    vars:
      ansible_connection: local
      ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ansible_playbook_python}}"
```

This ensures the local connection and the same Python as `ansible-playbook` are used.

If you add a `localhost` entry to your inventory, all implicit behavior is dropped and it is treated like any other host: group and host vars apply, including connection vars and `ansible_python_interpreter`. That also affects `delegate_to: localhost` and `local_action`.
